note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Quadratic upper bound (QUB) loss for fast adversarial training and its empirical effect on robustness and loss-landscape flatness

nodes.name: Adversarial training is costly
nodes.description: Adversarial training (AT) with multi-step attacks like PGD generates strong examples but requires substantial computation and long training time.

nodes.name: FAT trades exploration for speed
nodes.description: Fast adversarial training uses single-step attacks, allowing only coarse exploration of the adversarial space, and often suffers catastrophic overfitting, where robustness to PGD drops dramatically.

nodes.name: Goal: better loss without stronger inner maximization
nodes.description: The paper aims to improve FAT robustness through a new loss function rather than stronger inner maximization, keeping training short.

nodes.name: Quadratic upper bound on AT loss
nodes.description: Using convexity of cross-entropy w.r.t. logits, the AT loss is upper-bounded by L(f(x)) + (f(x+d)-f(x))^T grad_f L(f(x)) + (||H||_2/2)||f(x+d)-f(x)||^2 (Lemma 1).

nodes.name: Hessian norm bound
nodes.description: The Hessian norm of the cross-entropy loss w.r.t. logits satisfies ||H||_2 <= 1/2 (Lemma 2).

nodes.name: QUB loss definition
nodes.description: The QUB loss is L_QUB = L(f(x)) + (f(x+d)-f(x))^T grad_f L(f(x)) + (1/4)||f(x+d)-f(x)||^2, usable by simply replacing the loss in existing AT methods.

nodes.name: Clean-loss term drives standard accuracy
nodes.description: The first term of QUB, loss on clean samples, drives standard accuracy.

nodes.name: Second term flattens the landscape
nodes.description: The second term approximates d^T grad_x L(f(x)), the loss increment under perturbation; minimizing it dampens loss change and flattens the loss landscape.

nodes.name: Third term limits logit change
nodes.description: The third term, the squared change in logits under perturbation, limits the effect of adversarial examples on the output, as in earlier works such as TRADES.

nodes.name: Second term is cheaper than input-gradient form
nodes.description: Because grad_f L = softmax minus one-hot is closed-form and lives in R^C, the second QUB term needs no extra backprop and less memory than input-sized d^T grad_x L.

nodes.name: QUB over-regularizes clean accuracy
nodes.description: Because of its worst-case nature QUB yields larger gradients than the AT loss, and using it throughout can cause excessive regularization that degrades standard accuracy.

nodes.name: QUB-decreasing schedule
nodes.description: QUB-decreasing linearly transitions from QUB loss to AT loss over training (L_total = (1-lambda_t) L_QUB + lambda_t L_AT, lambda_t = t/T) to balance robustness and generalization.

nodes.name: QUB improves robustness of most FAT methods
nodes.description: Except for FGSM-RS, all baseline AT methods improve in robustness when QUB loss is applied (Table 1, CIFAR-10 ResNet18).

nodes.name: QUB-static vs decreasing trade-off
nodes.description: QUB-static achieves better robust accuracy than QUB-decreasing for most methods, but at larger standard accuracy cost, sometimes outweighing the robustness gain (e.g. Free-AT).

nodes.name: QUB-decreasing balances
nodes.description: QUB-decreasing achieves comparable or improved robust accuracy and better standard accuracy than QUB-static in many settings.

nodes.name: FGSM-RS is harmed
nodes.description: Combining QUB with FGSM-RS can degrade performance, because FGSM-RS's low-quality perturbations make QUB enforce smoothness in non-informative regions.

nodes.name: Modest training-time overhead
nodes.description: QUB adds slight training time over baselines but FAT with QUB remains cheaper than multi-step PGD-AT and TRADES.

nodes.name: Loss landscape is flatter with QUB
nodes.description: Loss-landscape visualizations show smoother landscapes with QUB (Fig 1), and the average dominant Hessian eigenvalue is smaller (Fig 2), with sparsity analysis in Fig 4, supporting the flattening explanation.

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet with ResNet18, WideResNet34-10 and PreActResNet18, SGD with lr 0.1, 100 epochs, on one RTX 4090.

isolated_nodes.name: FGSM limitations
isolated_nodes.description: FGSM adds perturbations of a fixed size epsilon in one step, failing to explore the adversarial space sufficiently, and FGSM-trained models lack robustness to PGD attacks.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the cost/overfitting problem of FAT, through the derived QUB bound and its interpretation, to the QUB-decreasing schedule, to empirical robustness and landscape-flatness evidence.
